A video of the Prime Minister promising money sounds like a dream, but it is becoming a digital nightmare. Scammers are using 'deepfakes'—AI-generated videos that look and sound exactly like real people—to trick you into giving away your hard-earned savings.

In this post, we break down:
• How to spot a fake video.
• Why 'processing fees' are a major red flag.
• The only place to verify government schemes.

Save this post to protect your family from financial fraud.

#CyberSecurity #DigitalSafety #FinancialLiteracy #DeepfakeAwareness #StayAlert

slides.title: If a 'free' government payout asks for an upfront fee, you are being scammed.
slides.body: Recent reports warn that scammers are using AI-generated deepfake videos of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to promote fake welfare schemes. If it looks too good to be true, it is.

slides.title: What is a Deepfake?
slides.content: A deepfake is a video where Artificial Intelligence (AI) is used to make a person say things they never said. Scammers use these to make it look like the Prime Minister is personally announcing a new cash benefit for you.

slides.title: The 'Processing Fee' Trap
slides.content: Reality: Real government welfare schemes never ask you to pay money to receive money. If a video asks for an 'advance processing fee' or 'registration charge' to unlock a benefit, it is a fraud.

slides.title: How Scammers Lure You
slides.content: 1. You see a video of a leader on social media. 2. The video promises quick cash or a new scheme. 3. You are directed to an external link. 4. You are asked to pay a fee or share bank details. 5. Your money is stolen.

slides.title: Checklist: Is it Official?
slides.content: Official Government Site? (Ends in .gov.in or .nic.in) [PASS/FAIL]. Does it ask for money upfront? [PASS/FAIL]. Is the video from a verified social media handle? [PASS/FAIL].

slides.title: Protect Your Savings
slides.cta_detail: Government schemes are announced through official gazettes and verified news channels, not through viral social media clips. Save this post to remind your family to verify before they click.
